body.p: Applicant presents all claims with status indicators in compliance with practice guidelines for making amendments under 37 C.F.R. §1.121(c)(1).Please amend the claims as follows:

br.br:
1. (Currently Amended) A system configured to determine concentrations of various gases using multiple gas sensors with one breath sample from a patient, the system comprising:a mouthpiece into which the patient blows;
a breath collector configured to receive the patient's breath through the mouthpiece coupled to the breath collector;
a gas inlet connectable to the breath collector;
a gas exhaust;
a manifold comprising a gas flow path in gaseous communication with the gas inlet and the gas exhaust;
the multiple gas sensors configured to measure concentrations of various gases including CH4, C02, H2, and H2S at once with the one breath sample, each gas sensor configured to output sensor data relating to a concentration of a different gas passing through the gas flow path, wherein the multiple gas sensors comprise a CH4 sensor, a C02 sensor, an H2 sensor, and an H2S sensor,
wherein the CH4 sensor is separate from the manifold, and wherein the C02 sensor, the H2 sensor, and the H2S sensor are positioned in series along the gas flow path comprising a single channel in the manifold;
a heating element in thermal communication with the manifold;
a temperature sensor configured to output temperature data relating to a temperature of the manifold;
a control system comprising one or more processors and a memory for determining concentrations of gases based on the output sensor data, the output sensor data comprising data output from the CH4 sensor, the C02 sensor, the H2 sensor, and the H2S sensor; and
a display that outputs the determined concentration of gases.

3. (Canceled)
4. (Previously Presented) The system of claim 3, wherein a first baffle is positioned adjacent to the H2 sensor and a second baffle is positioned adjacent to the H2S sensor and wherein the first and second baffles are sized and shaped to facilitate gas exchange with the H2S sensor and the H2 sensor.
5. (Original) The system of claim 1, further comprising a pump configured to pump gas through the gas flow path based on feedback from a flow meter configured to detect a flow rate through the gas flow path.
6. (Original) The system of claim 1, wherein the temperature sensor is a thermistor connected to a printed circuit board.
7. (Original) The system of claim 6, wherein the heating element is connected to the printed circuit board.
8. (Original) The system of claim 6, wherein the heating element comprises a trace printed on the printed circuit board.
9. (Original) The system of claim 4, wherein the heating element comprises a plurality of heating elements, and wherein each of the plurality of heating elements is configured to heat one of a set of zones of the manifold.
10. (Original) The system of claim 9, wherein the temperature sensor comprises a plurality of temperature sensors and wherein each of the plurality of temperature sensors is configured to output temperature data relating to one of the set of zones of the manifold.
11. (Original) The system of claim 1, wherein the control system is configured to maintain a minimum temperature of the manifold by energizing the heating element based on data output from the temperature sensor.
12. (Original) The system of claim 1, wherein the manifold comprises a metal block and wherein the gas flow path is constructed through the metal block.
13. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the manifold comprises a thermally conductive material, stainless steel, or copper.
14. (Canceled)
15. (Original) The system of claim 1, wherein the gas flow path comprises a baffle positioned adjacent to the at least one gas sensor.
16. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 11, wherein the minimum temperature is 40degrees Celsius or between 38 and 41 degrees Celsius.
17. (Canceled)
18. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the control system is configured to determine an indication of whether the patient has small intestine bacterial overgrowth (SIBO) based on the output sensor data comprising the concentrations of CH4, CO2, H2, and H2S measured at once with the one breath sample received from the patient.
19. (Previously Presented) The system of claim 1, wherein integration of the manifold and the multiple gas sensors allows for measuring the concentrations of the various gases including CH4, CO2, H2, and H2S at once in the same system.
20. (Previously Presented) The system of claim 1, wherein the control system is further configured to output an indication of diarrhea of the patient if the output sensor data indicates an increase in H2S level.

(Currently Amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the control system is further configured to output a positive indication of SIBO [[if]]in response to the output sensor data indicates indicatingthat an H2S level increases increased and a CH4 and H2 breath gases levels did not increase during a lactulose breath test.
22. (Withdrawn - Currently Amended) A method of sensing gas concentrations in exhaled breath for small intestine bacterial overgrowth (SIBO) testing, the method performed by the system of claim 1 and comprising:receiving, by the breath collector, a single batch of exhaled breath from a patient via the mouthpiece;
heating, by the heating element, the single batch of exhaled breath to a temperature above 37 degrees Celsius while pumping the air through [[a]]the gas flow path at a constant flow rate;
sensing, by the CH4 sensor, CO2 sensor, H2 sensor, and H2S sensor, gas concentrations of CH4, CO2, H2, and H2S at once in the gasflow path to determine whether the patient has SIBO;
using a set of electrochemical sensors; anddisplaying, on the display, the gas concentrations.
